questions.q: What is the key difference between a requirement and a visual?
options: They are the same thing and can be defined in any order
A requirement describes a decision the dashboard needs to support; a visual is the chart chosen later to support it
A visual must always be defined before any requirement
Requirements only apply to executive dashboards, not other reports
questions.explain: Chapter 8's audience-first discipline applies here: requirements are about what decision the data needs to inform, not which chart type displays it — visuals come later, in Lesson 89.

questions.q: Why does this capstone project use a deliberately written scope before opening Power BI at all?
options: A written scope prevents the project from growing indefinitely and gives a concrete standard to check the finished dashboard against
Scope documents are required by Power BI before any file can be created
Scope only matters for projects with more than five stakeholders
Scope has no real purpose beyond formality
questions.explain: Writing scope down first prevents endless scope creep and provides a clear reference point for evaluating whether the finished project (Lesson 93) actually meets what was promised.

questions.q: Which AdventureWorksDW2014 tables does this capstone's scope explicitly rely on?
options: FactInternetSales, FactResellerSales, DimSalesTerritory, DimProduct/DimProductCategory/DimProductSubcategory, and DimDate
Tables from Northwind exclusively
No specific tables — the scope is intentionally left undefined
Only a single flat table with no relationships
questions.explain: The four requirements (regional performance, product profitability, reseller fulfillment, trend over time) map directly onto these fact and dimension tables in AdventureWorksDW2014.

questions.q: What was deliberately excluded from this capstone's scope?
options: Nothing was excluded — the scope covers every possible feature
All time-based trend analysis
Currency conversion for international sales, data sources outside AdventureWorksDW2014, and mobile-specific layout
All product-line data
questions.explain: Scoping means explicitly excluding things too — here, currency conversion, outside data sources, and mobile layout were cut so the project stays finishable within this chapter.

questions.q: Why does Lesson 84 have no actual Power BI screen to interact with?
options: Power BI Desktop was uninstalled for this lesson
Requirements-gathering happens before opening any tool — it's about the business conversation, not the software
There was no real content for this lesson
This lesson is only available in the Power BI service, not Desktop
questions.explain: Gathering and scoping requirements is deliberately tool-agnostic — it's the conversation and thinking that has to happen before any table gets imported.
